skill.name: database-migration-helper
skill.description: Creates database migration files that match project conventions for Prisma, Sequelize, Alembic, Knex, TypeORM, Django, Rails, and related tools.
skill.summary: Drafts framework-aware database migrations with naming, rollback, and safety guidance.
skill.author: CrazyDubya

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are markdown inline code, file names, schema examples, or JSDoc type imports and are false positives. Seven command examples in SKILL.md are confirmed medium risk because they run ORM or framework CLIs. These commands can execute project code and write migration files, but no prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Framework CLI commands can execute project-controlled code.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running npx, npm, python, alembic, or rails commands. Show the exact command and target directory first.

remediation.issue: Migration names are used as command arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Sanitize generated migration names to a conservative pattern such as lowercase letters, numbers, and underscores before passing them to shell commands.

remediation.issue: Database migration generation may be confused with applying migrations.
remediation.suggestion: Default to creating migration files only. Clearly separate generation commands from commands that apply changes to a database.

content.value_statement: Database schema changes can fail when migration style, naming, and rollback rules vary across frameworks. This skill identifies project conventions and drafts migrations with safety checks.
actual_capabilities: Detects migration tools by checking common project files and directories.
Reviews existing migrations to match naming, timestamps, file layout, and rollback style.
Drafts migration files for Prisma, Sequelize, Knex, TypeORM, Alembic, Django, Rails, Flyway, and Liquibase workflows.
Includes up and down operations when the framework supports reversible migrations.
Highlights data loss, table locking, dependency, and rollback concerns before finalizing changes.
Provides reusable templates for common table, column, index, and foreign key changes.
limitations: It cannot prove that a migration is safe for a production database.
It depends on existing project files to infer the correct framework conventions.
Some suggested framework commands may execute project code and require explicit review.
Generated migrations still need tests on development and staging databases.

use_cases.title: Add Feature Schema Changes
use_cases.description: Create a new migration for tables, columns, indexes, or relationships while matching the repository convention.

use_cases.title: Review Migration Safety
use_cases.description: Check a planned schema change for rollback coverage, data loss risk, table locks, and production deployment concerns.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Migrations
use_cases.description: Guide contributors toward consistent migration names, order, templates, and testing expectations across multiple frameworks.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple schema addition.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration that adds a nullable phone field to users. Follow the existing migration style in this repository.

prompt_templates.title: Add an Indexed Table
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with constraints and indexes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration for an audit_events table with user reference, event type, payload, timestamps, and useful indexes. Include rollback support.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Risky Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request that needs safety analysis before file changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review how this project handles migrations, then propose a safe plan to make orders.status required without losing existing data.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Production Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for staged rollout and operational safety.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production-safe migration plan for splitting users.full_name into first_name and last_name. Include backfill, rollback, and deployment sequencing.

output_examples.input: Add a unique email index to users.
output: Identifies the active migration framework and recent naming pattern.
Creates a migration with a unique users email index and matching rollback step.
Warns about duplicate existing emails before applying the unique constraint.

output_examples.input: Create a posts table linked to users.
output: Drafts a migration with a posts table, user foreign key, timestamps, and index choices.
Adds rollback operations in reverse dependency order.
Notes that parent tables should exist before foreign keys are created.

output_examples.input: Make a large table change safer for production.
output: Separates schema preparation, data backfill, validation, and cleanup into staged migrations.
Calls out lock, timeout, and rollback risks for review before deployment.

best_practices: Review generated migrations before running them against any shared database.
Test both apply and rollback paths on realistic development or staging data.
Use one clear purpose per migration and name it after the schema change.
anti_patterns: Do not combine unrelated schema and data changes in one migration.
Do not drop populated columns without a backup, deprecation plan, or explicit approval.
Do not run generated framework commands blindly in production environments.

faq.question: Which migration tools does this skill support?
faq.answer: It includes guidance for Prisma, Sequelize, Knex, TypeORM, Alembic, Django, Rails, Flyway, and Liquibase.

faq.question: Can it apply migrations to my database?
faq.answer: It can suggest framework commands, but database changes should run only after human review and environment confirmation.

faq.question: Does it create rollback steps?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks for down, downgrade, rollback, or reversible operations when the framework supports them.

faq.question: How does it choose a migration name?
faq.answer: It checks existing migration files and uses descriptive names that match timestamp or sequence conventions.

faq.question: Can it handle data migrations?
faq.answer: Yes, but it recommends separating data changes, using batches for large data sets, and testing with realistic volumes.

faq.question: Is it safe for production work?
faq.answer: It helps identify risks, but production migrations still need backups, staging tests, and database owner approval.
